assumptions: Single currency (INR); all money is Decimal, rounded half-up to 2 dp, matching both the platform and the bank.
Platform fee: 2.36% (2% MDR + 18% GST on the MDR, collapsed into one rate), rounded half-up once per line. Refunds carry no fee.
Business-day calendar: RBI holidays (Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti, Dussehra, Diwali / Bali Pratipada), Sundays, and the 2nd/4th Saturdays are non-working; the 1st/3rd/5th Saturdays are working days.
Settlement lag is 1-2 business days. When a ledger row has no bank line, the earliest lag consistent with that absence is used to compute its expected settle date for the timing_difference bucket.

Batch merchants settle one netted bank line per capture date. An unexplained batch diff is recomputed as the fee applied once to the batch gross; if that explains the diff exactly, the whole batch -- never a single line -- is flagged rounding_variance.
A ledger row that duplicates another (same merchant, same amount, within 10 minutes) where only one side ever settles is flagged duplicate; the settled side keeps its normal match.

A refund is matched like any other transaction via its own bank reference. If no originating sale exists anywhere in the ledger, it is flagged unmatched_refund even though it settled cleanly -- a zero-variance control exception, not a cash discrepancy.
Matching never reads ground_truth.json or any file outside the two input CSVs.
